errors.py:33-40: LLMBudgetExhaustedError is a dedicated LLMRunnerError subclass created precisely so budget stops route to recovery without message sniffing
findings.finding: The plan's step 3 asserts that exhaustion 'raises pydantic-ai UsageLimitExceeded -> interpret_failure ... raises LLMRunnerError -> CompletionAgentStep.run ... catches only UnretryableOutputError ... -> raise_completion_workflow_failure raises a bare LLMError. No verdict.' This is refuted by the shipped code: interpret_failure classifies UsageLimitExceeded into the dedicated LLMBudgetExhaustedError, and CompletionAgentStep.run ALREADY has `except LLMBudgetExhaustedError as primary_exc: return self._recover(...)`. So a step-budget/UsageLimitExceeded runaway is already routed into bounded recovery today — it does NOT fall through to a bare LLMError with diagnostic=null.
findings.location: Section 'The mechanism that turns a runaway into "no verdict"', item 3
scenarios: The plan's premise that a budget-exhausted verify 'died empty / no verdict' via a bare LLMError does not match the current control flow, which already recovers on LLMBudgetExhaustedError

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the two contradictory actuator statements under the active 'THE FIX' heading so the opening sentence describes ROUTING the detected runaway into the bounded recovery + tool-free finalizer (not withdrawing tools to land on the looped history), leaving only the WITHDRAWN block to describe the superseded 'withdraw tools' approach.

findings.finding: Instruction-locality risk: the active 'THE FIX' section opens with a superseded actuator instruction ('Withdraw tools when a runaway is detected, so the agent lands a verdict on the evidence it has') that a later subsection explicitly overrides ('That is superseded' -> route to the tool-free finalizer, not the poisoned history). The correct actuator (route to bounded recovery + finalizer) is stated several paragraphs after the wrong one, under the same active heading, adjacent to a deliberately-retained WITHDRAWN PLAN block. An executor skimming the FIX header could implement tool-withdrawal-on-the-looped-history — the exact behaviour the plan argues against.
findings.location: 'THE FIX: trigger the existing actuator on repetition' opening line vs 'On runaway detection, ROUTE TO THE TOOL-FREE FINALIZER'
scenarios: An executor reads the FIX heading + first sentence and wires the toolset-filter predicate to withdraw tools in place, landing a verdict on the looped history — reintroducing the 'worse verdict on degraded evidence' the plan set out to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the FIX opening sentence to: 'On runaway detection, raise a typed runaway error that routes into the shipped bounded recovery + tool-free finalizer so the verdict is built from fresh per-criterion evidence, never the looped history. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] recompute the once-per-run_step cost/memoisation model against `_SteeringToolset.call_tool` (invoked per executed tool CALL, not per registered tool at request-build) and re-anchor the AC's invocation-count assertion to that seam's real firing pattern
evidence: Plan: 'Measured in E5: with 6 tools registered the predicate was invoked 6 times per run step (30 calls across 5 steps)' — this is the filter predicate evaluated per registered tool.
AC line: 'a test asserts the number of signature computations is <= the number of run steps, given a tool surface of 6 tools (measured: the predicate is invoked once per tool per step)'.

Shipped seam (e1b1) is `call_tool`, which fires per executed tool call: 6 registered tools does not imply 6 invocations per step when the model issues a different number of calls (the runaway traces issue ~1-3 calls/request).
EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified — the invocation seam exists but its per-step firing count under call_tool is unconfirmed.
findings.finding: The cost/memoisation analysis and its AC ('predicate runs ONCE PER TOOL PER STEP', 'invoked 6 times per run step (30 calls across 5 steps)', test asserts computations <= run steps 'given a tool surface of 6 tools') are derived from the `.filtered()` predicate's invocation model, which is evaluated per registered tool at request-build time. Post-e1b1 the seam is `_SteeringToolset.call_tool`, invoked once per actual tool CALL executed — not once per registered tool per request-build. The invocation count, and therefore the memoisation key/assertion, are specified against the wrong invocation model for the shipped mechanism.
findings.location: Cost: the predicate runs ONCE PER TOOL PER STEP section; AC 'the discriminator is computed at most ONCE per run_step'
scenarios: A request that issues 3 tool calls invokes call_tool 3 times, not 6; a step with 0 tool calls invokes it 0 times — so 'memoise on run_step' may under- or over-fire relative to the '6 tools' fixture, and the '<= run steps' assertion may pass offline yet mis-model production cost.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] the raised typed runaway error carries its own diagnostic (distinct_ratio_window and top repeated signatures) attached in interpret_failure's typed branch, mirroring LLMBudgetExhaustedError's budget_diag, so the trigger is recorded even when recovery succeeds
evidence: structured_run.py:95-101 shows LLMBudgetExhaustedError carries budget_diag attached in interpret_failure; the plan's new runaway branch has no analogous diagnostic-attachment requirement
AC3 asserts only that the runaway is NOT reported as 'the LLM provider call failed'; the distinct_ratio_window/top-signature diagnostic is pinned only in AC9's recovery-failure path
findings.finding: The plan pins the runaway diagnostic (distinct_ratio_window + top repeated signatures) only on the terminal gate_error_v1 sidecar path, but does not require the raised typed runaway error to carry that diagnostic through interpret_failure's new typed branch. The established pattern (errors.py:29-46; LLMBudgetExhaustedError attaches budget_diag at structured_run.py:95-101) is that interpret_failure attaches the diagnostic on the raised typed error itself; without pinning this for the runaway branch, a runaway routed to a SUCCESSFUL recovery still leaves the interpret_failure classification carrying only generic counters, not the runaway shape that triggered it.
findings.location: AC list, 'runaway error is classified by interpret_failure' (AC3) vs. fallback-diagnostic AC (AC9); THE FIX / actuator section
scenarios: A runaway trips the guard, recovery succeeds and lands a verdict, but the run-shape/audit record of WHY recovery ran carries only generic budget counters, not the distinct_ratio_window value and top repeated signature that actually fired
findings.suggested_fix: In interpret_failure's new runaway branch, attach the repetition summary to the typed error's .diagnostic the same way the UsageLimitExceeded branch attaches budget_diag, and add an AC asserting the classified runaway error carries distinct_ratio_window.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] re-frame E1 (or add evidence) so the schema-valid-landing claim is grounded in the CURRENT steering mechanism (non-empty advertised tools + synthetic steering results), not the retired `.filtered()` empty-surface `[...,0]` path that e1b1 proved 400s on Bedrock/Anthropic
evidence: Plan E1: 'with tool_step_limit=6 the tool surface offered per request went [6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 0]' — the trailing 0 is the emptied surface.

e1b1 (closed, verified): 'When the filter trips after any tool call has occurred, pydantic-ai omits tools/toolConfig from the next request ... Bedrock Converse rejects that request: ValidationException 400' — i.e. the [...,0] shape is provider-broken; e1b1 replaced it so 'tool definitions stay advertised for the whole run'.
EVIDENCE CLASS: Contradicted (for the live provider path) — the observed E1 mechanism is the one e1b1 removed as provider-invalid.
findings.finding: E1's observed tool surface `[6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 0]` (surface emptied to 0 on the landing turn) is the pre-e1b1 `.filtered()` behaviour — the exact empty-tool-surface-over-toolUse-history shape that the plan's own closed dependency e1b1 proved returns a Bedrock/Anthropic 400 live. Under the current steering mechanism the surface never drops to 0. E1 therefore no longer demonstrates the landing behaviour of the shipped code, so its retirement of the 9a08 'unparseable prose' objection rests on a mechanism that is not the one now in production.
scenarios: Reviewers/implementers treat E1 as proof the landing turn is schema-valid on the real provider, but E1 used the emptied-surface path; on Bedrock/Anthropic that path 400s, and the actual landing now happens via steered non-empty tool results — a materially different turn whose schema-validity E1 did not observe.

EVIDENCE CLASS: Partially-verified — pydantic-ai WrapperToolset/call_tool exist and are used in-repo, but exception propagation from THIS seam out of agent.run_sync is unconfirmed post-e1b1.
findings.finding: The E5 feasibility experiment — that a raise from the toolset filter predicate propagates cleanly out of agent.run_sync and survives in __cause__ — was measured against the `.filtered(lambda ctx, _: ctx.run_step <= limit)` predicate seam, which the plan's own closed dependency rebar:e1b1-859e-a7b4-48f2 has REPLACED with a `_SteeringToolset(WrapperToolset).call_tool` override (verified at src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py:45-65). The actuator must raise from the current `call_tool` seam, not the retired filter predicate, and exception propagation from `call_tool` out of agent.run_sync (and into the __cause__ chain interpret_failure inspects) is not re-verified against the shipped mechanism.
findings.location: Feasibility — MEASURED (E5 bullet); THE FIX / actuator section; dep rebar:e1b1-859e-a7b4-48f2
scenarios: The runaway detector raises its typed error from _SteeringToolset.call_tool; pydantic-ai handles a tool-execution exception differently from a toolset-filter exception (e.g. wraps/retries/swallows it), so it never reaches interpret_failure and the route-to-recovery AC silently fails at runtime.
The steering wrapper's past-limit branch returns a notice WITHOUT calling the wrapped tool — the actuator must decide whether to raise before or instead of that branch, which E5 never exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the E5 bullet and the actuator section to hook the raise into `_SteeringToolset.call_tool` (agent_call.py:59-62), and add/re-record an experiment showing the exception survives from that override; state explicitly whether the runaway check runs before the `ctx.run_step > limit` steering branch or on every call.
